status.notChecked: Rook has not checked Ceph's health yet.
status.staleWhy_one: Rook checks every minute by default, so for more than {{count}} minute this status has not been refreshed: the Rook operator may not be running.
status.staleWhy_other: Rook checks every minute by default, so for more than {{count}} minutes this status has not been refreshed: the Rook operator may not be running.

status.mixedVersions_other: The daemons run {{count}} Ceph versions ({{versions}}): an upgrade is under way, or stuck.
status.noToolbox: No toolbox runs here. Rook's `deploy/examples/toolbox.yaml` starts one; then Shell on its pod runs `ceph status`, `ceph health detail` and the like. This extension runs no commands itself.
status.toolbox: Toolbox: {{pod}}. Shell on its pod runs `ceph status`, `ceph health detail` and the like; this extension runs no commands itself.

metrics.noSeries: The Prometheus-compatible source has no Ceph metrics with namespace="{{namespace}}". Rook's CephCluster sets them up with spec.monitoring.enabled and the Prometheus Operator's ServiceMonitor for the mgr.
storage.noBucketClass: No StorageClass provisions buckets in this object store.

checks.MON_DOWN.meaning: One or more monitors are down; the cluster keeps working while a majority of monitors is up.
checks.MON_DOWN.next: Look at the rook-ceph-mon pods on the Daemons tab.
checks.MON_CLOCK_SKEW.meaning: The clocks of the monitors' nodes differ by more than Ceph allows.
checks.MON_CLOCK_SKEW.next: Check time synchronisation (NTP, chrony) on the nodes running monitors.
checks.MON_DISK_LOW.meaning: A monitor's disk is nearly full.
checks.MON_DISK_LOW.next: Free space under the cluster's dataDirHostPath on the monitor's node.
checks.MON_DISK_CRIT.meaning: A monitor's disk is critically full; the monitor will stop when it runs out.
checks.MON_DISK_CRIT.next: Free space under the cluster's dataDirHostPath on the monitor's node now.
checks.MON_MSGR2_NOT_ENABLED.meaning: Some monitors do not listen on the newer msgr2 protocol.
checks.MGR_DOWN.meaning: No manager is active: metrics, the dashboard and Rook's orchestration stop.
checks.MGR_MODULE_DEPENDENCY.meaning: A manager module cannot run because something it needs is missing.
checks.OSD_DOWN.meaning: One or more OSDs are down: their data is served by the other copies while they are.
checks.OSD_DOWN.next: Look at the rook-ceph-osd pods and their nodes on the Daemons tab.
checks.OSD_HOST_DOWN.meaning: Every OSD of a host is down.
checks.OSD_HOST_DOWN.next: Check that node and its disks.
checks.OSD_ROOT_DOWN.meaning: Every OSD under a CRUSH root is down.
checks.OSD_ORPHAN.meaning: An OSD is in the CRUSH map but does not exist.
checks.OSD_OUT_OF_ORDER_FULL.meaning: The OSD fullness thresholds are not in ascending order.
checks.OSD_NEARFULL.meaning: One or more OSDs are nearly full.
checks.OSD_NEARFULL.next: Add capacity or delete data before they reach the full ratio, when writes stop.
checks.OSD_BACKFILLFULL.meaning: One or more OSDs are too full to take data moved to them by backfill.
checks.OSD_FULL.meaning: One or more OSDs are full: Ceph stops writes to the pools on them.
checks.OSD_FULL.next: Add capacity or delete data at once.
checks.OSD_FLAGS.meaning: OSD flags such as noout or noup are set on some OSDs, hosts or classes.
checks.OSDMAP_FLAGS.meaning: Cluster-wide flags such as noout, norebalance or pause are set; they are often left over from maintenance.
checks.OSD_UPGRADE_FINISHED.meaning: Every OSD runs the new release, but require-osd-release still names an old one.
checks.OSD_FILESTORE.meaning: Some OSDs still use FileStore, which newer Ceph releases do not run.
checks.OSD_SLOW_PING_TIME_FRONT.meaning: Network pings between OSDs on the public network are slow.
checks.OSD_SLOW_PING_TIME_BACK.meaning: Network pings between OSDs on the cluster network are slow.
checks.OSD_TOO_MANY_REPAIRS.meaning: An OSD repaired more read errors than Ceph allows: its disk may be failing.
checks.TOO_FEW_OSDS.meaning: The cluster has fewer OSDs than the pools' replica size needs.
checks.BLUESTORE_SLOW_OP_ALERT.meaning: BlueStore on some OSDs reports slow operations: a disk may be slow or failing.
checks.BLUESTORE_SPURIOUS_READ_ERRORS.me: Some OSDs saw read errors that went away on retry: a disk may be failing.
checks.BLUESTORE_NO_PER_POOL_OMAP.meanin: Some OSDs were created before per-pool omap accounting.
checks.BLUEFS_SPILLOVER.meaning: The OSD's metadata no longer fits on its fast device and spills onto the slow one.
checks.BLUEFS_LOW_SPACE.meaning: The OSD's metadata device is running out of space.
checks.DEVICE_HEALTH.meaning: A disk is expected to fail soon, by its SMART data.
checks.DEVICE_HEALTH_IN_USE.meaning: A disk expected to fail soon still holds data.
checks.PG_AVAILABILITY.meaning: Some placement groups are inactive: reads and writes to the data in them block.
checks.PG_AVAILABILITY.next: Usually OSDs are down; look at OSD_DOWN first.
checks.PG_DEGRADED.meaning: Some data has fewer copies than its pool asks for; Ceph recovers it when it can.
checks.PG_DEGRADED.next: Usually OSDs are down or recovering.
checks.PG_RECOVERY_FULL.meaning: Data cannot recover because OSDs are full.
checks.PG_BACKFILL_FULL.meaning: Data cannot move because OSDs are too full for backfill.
checks.PG_DAMAGED.meaning: Scrubbing found inconsistent data in some placement groups.
checks.OBJECT_UNFOUND.meaning: Ceph knows objects exist but finds no copy of them.
checks.OBJECT_MISPLACED.meaning: Some objects are not where CRUSH places them yet; Ceph is moving them.
checks.PG_NOT_SCRUBBED.meaning: Some placement groups were not scrubbed in time.
checks.PG_NOT_DEEP_SCRUBBED.meaning: Some placement groups were not deep-scrubbed in time.
checks.RECENT_CRASH.meaning: Ceph daemons crashed recently; the crashes stay listed until someone archives them.
checks.RECENT_CRASH.next: In the toolbox, `ceph crash ls` lists them.
checks.SLOW_OPS.meaning: Some requests to OSDs or monitors are taking long.
checks.POOL_FULL.meaning: A pool reached its quota: writes to it stop.
checks.POOL_NEAR_FULL.meaning: A pool is near its quota.
checks.POOL_NO_REDUNDANCY.meaning: A pool keeps a single copy of its data: losing one OSD loses data.
checks.POOL_APP_NOT_ENABLED.meaning: A pool has no application (rbd, cephfs, rgw) set.
checks.POOL_TOO_FEW_PGS.meaning: A pool has fewer placement groups than its data needs.
checks.POOL_TOO_MANY_PGS.meaning: A pool has more placement groups than its data needs.
checks.TOO_MANY_PGS.meaning: The OSDs hold more placement groups each than Ceph allows.
checks.POOL_TARGET_SIZE_BYTES_OVERCOMMIT: The pools' target sizes add up to more than the cluster holds.
checks.FS_DEGRADED.meaning: A filesystem is degraded: one of its ranks is not active.
checks.FS_WITH_FAILED_MDS.meaning: A filesystem has a failed metadata server rank.
checks.MDS_ALL_DOWN.meaning: No metadata server of a filesystem is up: the filesystem cannot be used.
checks.MDS_INSUFFICIENT_STANDBY.meaning: Fewer standby metadata servers are available than the filesystem asks for.
checks.MDS_SLOW_REQUEST.meaning: Some metadata requests are taking long.
checks.MDS_SLOW_METADATA_IO.meaning: A metadata server waits long for its own metadata reads and writes.
checks.MDS_CLIENT_LATE_RELEASE.meaning: Clients do not release capabilities the metadata server asked back.
checks.MDS_CLIENT_RECALL.meaning: Clients do not release cached inodes the metadata server asked back.
checks.MDS_TRIM.meaning: A metadata server's journal is falling behind.
checks.MDS_CACHE_OVERSIZED.meaning: A metadata server's cache is over its memory limit.
checks.MDS_DAMAGE.meaning: A metadata server found damaged metadata.
checks.AUTH_INSECURE_GLOBAL_ID_RECLAIM.m: Clients reconnect in a way that has a known security problem.
checks.AUTH_INSECURE_GLOBAL_ID_RECLAIM_A: Ceph still lets clients reconnect in a way that has a known security problem.
checks.AUTH_BAD_CAPS.meaning: Some keys have capabilities Ceph cannot parse.
checks.next.toolbox: In the toolbox, `ceph health detail` lists what it is about.
change.conflict: The object changed since it was read. Open it again to see the change, then try again.
manage.muteFull_one: Rook mutes at most {{count}} health check.
manage.muteFull_other: Rook mutes at most {{count}} health checks.
manage.pausedText: Rook does not reconcile this while the label ceph.rook.io/do-not-reconcile is set: changes to it wait.
manage.restarted: Deleted: its controller starts a new one.
manage.toolboxDeployed: Deployed: its pod starts in a moment.
manage.toolboxNoContainer: The toolbox Deployment has no rook-ceph-tools container: update it by hand.
manage.toolboxOld: The toolbox runs {{image}}, not the cluster's Ceph image.
upgrade.intro: Rook upgrades Ceph daemon by daemon, waiting after each one until the cluster settles. It refuses to start while Ceph reports HEALTH_ERR. Read Rook's Ceph upgrade guide before upgrading.
upgrade.unchanged: Enter the image to upgrade to.
upgrade.blocked: Upgrading is not possible until the blocking checks pass.
upgrade.check.badImage: This is not an image reference such as quay.io/ceph/ceph:v20.2.4-20260818.
upgrade.check.noVersion: The image's tag names no Ceph version (vX, vX.Y.Z or vX.Y.Z-date).
upgrade.check.unsupported: Ceph {{version}} is not a release this Rook supports (Squid v19 and Tentacle v20).
upgrade.check.tooOld: Ceph {{version}} is older than {{from}}, the first {{release}} version this Rook supports.
upgrade.check.notRecommended: Ceph {{version}} is not recommended: it has a known data corruption issue with read affinity.
upgrade.check.downgrade: Ceph {{version}} is older than the running {{current}}: Ceph is never downgraded.
upgrade.check.majorJump: From {{current}} to {{version}} skips a major release: upgrade one release at a time.
upgrade.check.healthError: Ceph reports HEALTH_ERR: Rook refuses to start an upgrade.
upgrade.check.healthWarn: Ceph reports HEALTH_WARN: look at the health checks before upgrading.
upgrade.check.mixedVersions: The daemons run {{count}} different Ceph versions: an upgrade is still under way.
upgrade.check.otherRegistry: Rook supports only the official images from quay.io/ceph/ceph.
upgrade.check.majorTag: The tag names only a major version: production clusters should use a full version and build tag.
pool.intro: Settings of the Ceph pool {{pool}}. Rook applies them to Ceph.
pool.sizeHint: At least 3 in production; 1 keeps a single copy.
pool.erasureCoded: An erasure-coded pool: its layout cannot change.
pool.quotaHint: A quantity such as 100Gi; empty removes the quota.
pool.placementWarning: Changing the failure domain, device class or root makes Ceph move the pool's data.
pool.badSize: The size is a whole number from 1 to 9.
pool.badQuantity: The quota is a quantity such as 100Gi.
pool.badObjects: The object quota is a whole number above 0.
pool.badCrushName: CRUSH names use letters, digits, '-', '_' and '.'.
mds.intro: Metadata servers of this filesystem: how many are active, and whether each has a standby with a warm cache.
mds.activeHint: 1 to 50; one more than you need gives no benefit.
mds.activeStandby: Keep a standby with a warm cache for each active one
mds.badCount: The number of active metadata servers is 1 to 50.
gateways.intro: How many RGW pods serve this object store.
gateways.badCount: The number of instances is 1 to 100.
storageClass.intro: A StorageClass that provisions volumes or buckets here, as Rook's examples write it.
storageClass.name: StorageClass name
delete.dataWarning: Rook deletes the Ceph objects behind it, and their data, unless they are set to be preserved.
delete.classesOn: StorageClasses put data here: {{classes}}. Delete them first.
create.title: Create
create.intro: New pools, filesystems, object stores and users, as Rook's examples write them. The YAML is shown before it is applied.
create.name: Name
create.failureOsd: osd: copies on different disks (test clusters)
create.withClass: Also create a StorageClass on it
create.done: Applied: Rook creates it in a moment.
create.badName: A name is lowercase letters, digits, '-' and '.'.
create.noStore: This cluster has no object store.
create.noOperator: The Rook operator was not found: the CSI drivers' names are not known.
osds.treeHint: Where Rook placed each OSD, from the labels on its Deployment. After a change made with `ceph osd crush` in the toolbox, `ceph osd tree` is the truth.
osds.noMetrics: Up/in and usage need the Ceph mgr's and Rook's exporter metrics in a Prometheus-compatible source.
osds.removeIntro: Removes osd.{{id}} from Ceph with Rook's purge Job (`rook ceph osd remove`, not forced): Rook refuses when the OSD is not safe to destroy. Remove one OSD at a time and wait for the data to rebalance.
osds.removeHost: Afterwards, wipe or remove the disk, or leave it out of the cluster's device selection: otherwise Rook creates an OSD on it again.
osds.removePvc: Lower the device set's count first, or Rook creates an OSD for the set again; the Job deletes the OSD's claim.
osds.pgsNotClean: Not every placement group is active+clean: removing an OSD now risks data.
osds.pgsUnknown: The placement groups' state is not known (no metrics): check `ceph status` in the toolbox first.
osds.noRookImage: The Rook operator's image was not found: the purge Job needs it.
osds.jobHint: Open a Job to see its pod's logs.
osds.storageIntro: Which devices Rook turns into OSDs, and what it may change on existing ones.
osds.deviceFilterHint: A regular expression of device names such as ^sd[b-z]; empty removes it.
osds.allowDeviceClassUpdate: Apply a node's device class to its existing OSDs
osds.allowDeviceClassUpdateHint: Changing an OSD's device class makes Ceph move the data of pools that use it.
osds.allowOsdCrushWeightUpdate: Raise an OSD's CRUSH weight when its disk grows
osds.autoRemove: Remove OSDs that are out and safe to remove
osds.autoRemoveHint: Keep off while replacing disks by annotation: Rook's replacement needs it off.
osds.deviceSetsHint: OSDs on volumes: Rook creates as many as each set's count.
osds.badCount: The count is a whole number from 0 to 1000.
osds.toolboxOnly: Moving buckets, reweighting and marking OSDs out or in are not done through Rook's objects: run `ceph osd crush move`, `ceph osd reweight` or `ceph osd out` in the toolbox.
topology.intro: Where Rook places this node's OSDs in the CRUSH map, and their device class. Empty removes a label.
topology.existingOsds: Rook applies a topology change to OSDs created afterwards. Existing OSDs move only when the node is removed from the cluster and added again, node by node.
topology.deviceClass: Device class of every OSD on the node
topology.classApplies: A CephCluster applies device classes to existing OSDs: their data moves.
topology.classNew: A device class reaches existing OSDs only with the cluster's "Apply a node's device class to its existing OSDs".
topology.classOwned: {{clusters}} gives this node its own device class: Rook skips a node that also has the label.
topology.classConflict: {{clusters}} already gives this node a device class: remove it there first.
topology.badName: {{value}} is not a CRUSH name: letters, digits, '-', '_' and '.'.
